sketches.title: The House That Misplaced Itself
sketches.premise: You are moving house one box at a time, but each box changes what the new home can be. Say what happens next as the move slowly becomes a very different kind of move. Keep it clear, useful, and just a little cursed.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that each move is one new, practical change caused by the box just handled, fits every earlier change, does not skip the needed unpacking or setup, does not declare the move finished, and does not restore an earlier arrangement.
sketches.move_shape: Start with “Then” and name one box action plus its plain result; for example: “Then the box marked KITCHEN is opened, and it contains a working fog machine, so the new kitchen fills with mist.”
sketches.first_card: Then the first box is opened: it is marked “LAMPS,” and it contains one very bright desk lamp.

sketches.title: The Floor Plan Has Opinions
sketches.premise: A moving crew places boxes in a new house while you discover what each room is really for. Every move adds one box and one small change to the floor plan, until the house has a strange but usable purpose. Be helpful first; the house will supply the roast.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the move places or opens exactly one box, creates one new room fact because of that placement, fits the whole floor plan, does not jump past moving or arranging steps, does not finish the house, and does not undo a placement.
sketches.move_shape: Name one box and where it goes, then the immediate room change; for example: “Then the box of bath towels goes in the study, so the study now has a soft wall around the desk.”
sketches.first_card: Then the box marked “BOOKS” is carried into the empty front room and set beside the window.

sketches.title: Please Do Not Shake the Future
sketches.premise: You are moving a house full of ordinary boxes, and each one reveals a true but awkward detail about the people who lived there. Take the move from packing to unpacking without inventing a whole new life in one leap. The truth may be kind, rude, or both.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that each move opens or handles one box and reveals one new fact caused by that handling, fits all revealed facts, does not skip from clue to full confession, does not end the move or solve every problem, and does not erase a fact already learned.
sketches.move_shape: Start with “Then” and give the box action followed by the immediate clue; for example: “Then the box marked ‘WINTER CLOTHES’ is opened, and every coat has the same hotel key in its pocket.”
sketches.first_card: Then a small box marked “MISC.” is opened, and inside is a neatly wrapped silver spoon.

sketches.title: The Welcome Committee
sketches.premise: You are moving into a house whose rooms, objects, and neighbors quietly make rules. Each box gives the household one new rule that must be obeyed from then on. Make the rules grow stranger, not impossible; the last player standing gets to be smug about the furniture.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that each move handles one box and causes one clear new household rule, that the rule fits every earlier rule, that no rule is introduced without the box causing it, that the move does not declare the house settled, and that it does not cancel or reverse a standing rule.
sketches.move_shape: Name one box, the event that opens it, and the rule it creates; for example: “Then the box of plates is unpacked, and from now on every meal must be eaten while standing on one foot.”
sketches.first_card: Then the box marked “HOUSE KEYS” is opened, and the smallest key fits the back door.

sketches.title: The Packing List Fights Back
sketches.premise: Two movers check boxes against a shared list, but every item creates a new problem that must be handled before the next one can matter. The goal is not to wreck the house at random; it is to make one honest bad idea lead to another. The host will explain the mess like it was always obvious.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that each move concerns one listed box or item and produces one immediate problem caused by it, respects the full inventory and earlier fixes, does not skip from object to catastrophe, does not finish the move, and does not pretend a problem was never there.
sketches.move_shape: Start with “Then,” name the box or item, and give the next practical problem; for example: “Then the box marked ‘MIRRORS’ is opened, and one mirror reflects a room that is not in the house.”
sketches.first_card: Then the box marked “CUPS” is opened, and it contains twelve cups but only eleven handles.

sketches.title: Unpacking the Wrong House
sketches.premise: A house mover opens boxes in order, and each box changes the identity of one room. Build a clear chain from ordinary move to wildly unsuitable home, while keeping every change tied to the box just opened. Do not leap to the punchline; even a haunted pantry has paperwork.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that each move opens exactly one box and changes exactly one room because of it, fits the room’s full history and the whole house, does not skip the physical change that explains the result, does not declare the house complete, and does not turn a room back into an earlier version.
sketches.move_shape: Name the box, the room it affects, and the one immediate change; for example: “Then the box marked ‘GARDEN TOOLS’ is opened in the hallway, and the hallway grows a narrow strip of soil.”
sketches.first_card: Then the first box, marked “DOORMAT,” is opened in the entryway, and the mat reads: “Welcome, staff.”
